ENERGY SHIELD + HEALTH PICKUP
================================================

Two Models for Teammates
  EnergyShield.fbx    Cyan energy shield: hexagonal grid, metal frame, and rear grip.
  HealthPickup.fbx    Orange-red health capsule: white front cross, glowing side compartments, and charge bars.

Both files are standalone Static Meshes without skeletons or animations.
Units: centimeters. Import scale: 1. Forward: -Y; up: +Z.
Shield: approximately 116 x 32 x 152 cm, with origin at the shield face center for attachment to a hand or character.
Health pickup: approximately 35 x 30 x 47 cm, with origin at the bottom center for placement as a pickup.
Scale the health pickup in-game as needed; for example, scale 0.5 makes it approximately 24 cm tall.

Unreal Import
-------------
1. Drag both FBXs into the Content Browser, import as Static Meshes, and set scale to 1.
2. Enable Import Materials / Import Textures as needed.
   Each FBX embeds four textures, also available for manual import from the textures folder.
3. Both models share M_Props_Atlas. Reuse the first model's material on the second to avoid duplicates.
   Material connections:
     Props_BaseColor.png -> Base Color (sRGB on)
     Props_Emissive.png  -> Emissive Color (sRGB on; optionally multiply by 2-4)
     Props_Roughness.png -> Roughness (sRGB off)
     Props_Metallic.png  -> Metallic (sRGB off)
   The FBX importer may not connect every channel automatically. Connect Emissive manually if glow is missing.
4. The shield's second material slot, M_Shield_Field_Transparent, is an optional energy film.
   In Unreal, set Blend Mode = Translucent and Two Sided = enabled.
   Recommended Unlit setup: connect cyan (0.015, 0.21, 0.28) to Emissive, with Opacity = 0.20.
   For only the metal frame and open grid, set this material's Opacity to 0.
   Transparency and bloom are engine material/post-processing effects that require configuration in Unreal.
5. Set dynamic props to Movable. Add simple collision as needed: Box for the shield, Sphere for the health pickup.
   Blueprint components are convenient for collision control; the model files contain no collision meshes.

Connect to Existing Gameplay
----------------------------
Shield: attach the Static Mesh to a character or hand component and show it while Shield is active.
        Use your existing Blueprint for blocking, cooldown, durability, and hit feedback.
Health pickup: place it in a pickup Actor with Sphere Collision for Overlap.
        After confirming the player: Health = min(Health + HealAmount, MaxHealth), then destroy the pickup.
        For an idle effect, slowly rotate the Actor or make it float up and down.
These FBXs contain only models and materials; they do not execute healing or blocking logic.

Other Files
-----------
Shield_Health.blend                  Blender 4.5 source with packed textures.
textures/                           Four shared textures.
preview/Shield_Health_Preview.png    Actual Blender render; health pickup enlarged 3x to show detail.
source/build_props.py                Script to regenerate the models.
source/validate_exports.py           FBX reimport validation script.
model_manifest.json                 Dimensions, polygon counts, and material slot information.
validation_report.json              Actual validation results.

The Blender source's 01_ASSETS_REAL_SCALE collection retains both models at actual scale,
hidden by default to avoid overlapping the presentation scene. STUDIO_PREVIEW_ objects are preview-only.
To re-export, unhide and select only SM_EnergyShield or SM_HealthPickup,
enable Selected Objects, and exclude presentation stands, cameras, and preview copies.

Completed Blender FBX reimport checks cover triangles, UVs, dimensions, origins, closed meshes, and embedded textures.
Actual runtime testing in Unreal Engine has not been performed. These models are original stylized prototypes created for this delivery.
